table.title: Bank-Note Issues of Modern Chinese Banks, 1921-1935
footnotes: Note.—With the nationalization of silver and the change of China's currency system, on November 3, 1935, the privilege of note issue was taken from the Chinese commercial banks. From that time onward only the three Government banks were to issue notes, while the circulation of the eight commercial banks was to be withdrawn within two years. This means that since the beginning of November, 1935, there was no more issue department in commercial banks (Shanghai), and the figures cited here as of end of December, 1935, are actually applicable to the beginning of November, from which date onward the Government banks were responsible for those issues.
